latest.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade the measures her Department is taking, through its foreign policy and Irish aid programme, to respond to the growing influence of anti-rights movements globally, particularly those seeking to undermine gender equality and women's rights; and whether additional policy or funding measures are being considered to support women's rights organisations and movements responding to these threats.
latest.reply:
The Government remains firmly committed to advancing gender equality and protecting human rights internationally. We recognise gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls as a fundamental human right and a strategic imperative.
The global pushback against gender equality poses a significant challenge to strengthening gender perspectives and women’s empowerment globally. It threatens an unacceptable rollback of core values and progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals, while making it increasingly difficult to advance a rights-based approach in external action.
As human rights and gender equality face serious levels of opposition globally, leadership is needed now more than ever in defending and promoting fundamental human rights, including gender equality, women’s and girls’ empowerment, and sexual and reproductive health and rights. Ireland is deeply concerned by growing global challenges in these areas and continues to advocate internationally for them.
Reductions in international development budgets risk undermining progress on gender equality. We believe it is important to protect resources for gender equality, including support for women-led and women's rights organisations at the frontline of humanitarian and development responses. In line with the Government's international development policy, A Better World, we provide direct funding for gender equality programmes to ensure integration of gender and women’s rights across all interventions.
Ireland

latest.question: Deputy Cathal Crowe asked the Minister for Education and Youth if she will intervene in the case of a constituent (details supplied) facing an unfair duplicate €440 registration fee from the Teaching Council due to protracted administrative delays; if the council has the power to issue manual fee waivers in such instances.
latest.reply:
The Teaching Council is the body with the statutory authority and responsibility for the regulation of the teaching profession in Ireland including the registration of teachers in the State.
The Teaching Council register teachers under the Teaching Council Act 2001-2015 and in line with the Teaching Council Registration Regulations 2025. Per the legislation, my department has no role in the registration of individual teachers.
In line with Section 23 (1) of the Teaching Council Act 2001-2015, the Council may determine fees, subject to the consent of the Minister, in relation to the performance of its functions, the provision of services and the carrying on of its activities.
The Recognition team at the Teaching Council have informed me that they will liaise with the applicant directly and they will advise him directly regarding his application.

latest.question: Deputy Mairéad Farrell asked the Minister for Education and Youth the work her Department is doing to ensure that school pupils in single-sex schools have access to a range of subject choices, and that subject choices available to pupils are not influenced by gender-stereotypes.
latest.reply:
My Department is committed to providing an education system that is inclusive, equitable, and empowering for all. Every learner deserves the opportunity to thrive. Our focus is on high standards, inclusive practices, and strong supports to ensure no one is left behind.
My Department’s work in this area includes the STEM Education Policy Statement 2017–2026, which aims to improve STEM experiences and outcomes for all learners, from early learning and care through to post-primary level. It acknowledges that there is a need to increase the uptake of STEM subjects and to enhance STEM learning for learners of all backgrounds, abilities and gender, with a particular focus on uptake by females
In addition, I announced the publication of subject and career information leaflets in September this year supports learners at the key transition to post-primary schools with information on subject choices, including STEM.
The range of subjects offered depends on each school’s resources, staffing, and student needs. Each school retains autonomy to design timetables and determine which programmes and subjects to provide. Schools aim to balance available resources with student demand. Any issues arising on the matter of subject provision and subject choice should be addressed to the principal of the school in question in the first instance.

latest.reply:

This NDP Sectoral Plan involves a very strong emphasis on maximising existing capacity and prioritisation of school building projects to meet the most urgent needs within the allocated capital funding across all schools in the country.
This allows my department to keep a strong focus on the provision of additional capacity to cater for demographics, new housing developments and the roll-out of additional special classes for children with additional needs. This approach reflects the department's fundamental objective of ensuring the availability of a school place for every child.

In this regard, there will continue to be a strong emphasis on maximising existing capacity across the school estate and also ensuring that school admissions policies and processes are targeted at meeting local mainstream and special class requirements.

latest.question: Deputy Séamus McGrath asked the Minister for Education and Youth if she will provide an update on the application for additional accommodation by a primary school (details supplied) in Cork.
latest.reply:
I can confirm that the department has received an application for capital funding under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme from the school referred to in September 2026. The application relates to a request for accommodation for a special education classroom and is currently under assessment.
My department is prioritising applications which relate to essential mainstream and special education accommodation. In assessing ASA applications, my department consider whether some or all of the requirements presented can be met within the school’s existing accommodation or accommodation available at other schools in the area. The team also review demographic and enrolment projections to consider the impact on accommodation requirements – for example, accommodation becoming available in the medium term due to decreasing enrolments.
I can confirm that an official acknowledged receipt of the school's application in September and a decision will issue to the school directly upon completion of the assessment process.

latest.question: Deputy Brian Brennan asked the Minister for Education and Youth the reason incremental credit has been refused to a person (details supplied); and if officials from her Department can meet with the applicant to resolve the issue.
latest.reply:
As the Deputy may be aware, the criteria for the award of incremental credit are set out in my Department's Circulars 10/2001 for primary teachers and 29/2007 and 29/2010 for post-primary teachers. These circulars provide for the award of incremental credit in respect of certain prior teaching service, including overseas teaching service.
There is no contractual entitlement to incremental credit. Applicants must submit a completed application for assessment and any award is determined in accordance with the agreed criteria set out in the relevant circulars.
The criteria for the award of incremental credit to recognised teachers were agreed under the auspices of the Teachers' Conciliation Council (TCC) and are subject to review through the established TCC mechanisms. Any changes to these criteria must be agreed through those arrangements.
In relation to the specific case referred to by the Deputy, a solicitor's letter was received by my Department while the case was under consideration by the independent Incremental Credit Appeals Committee. The Committee had previously deferred its consideration of the appeal to allow for the submission of additional information.
The Appeals Committee subsequently considered the case in October 2019 and upheld the Department's original decision. latest.question: Deputy Niamh Smyth asked the Minister for Education and Youth the supports available to schools experiencing significant educational disadvantage that do not currently have DEIS status; the options for such schools to access additional supports and resources; and the status of previously approved school building projects.
latest.reply:
Addressing educational disadvantage in all schools is a key priority for me as Minister for Education and Youth. The DEIS programme is targeted at schools with the highest levels of concentrated disadvantage. Schools that were included in the most recent expansion of the programme in 2022 were those with the highest levels of concentrated disadvantage as identified through the refined DEIS identification model. Schools were not required to apply for inclusion in the DEIS programme, and the model was applied fairly and equally to all schools. A detailed paper on the refined DEIS identification model is available on gov.ie.
Earlier this year, I announced the DEIS Strategy to 2035 which is the first long-term, whole-system approach to addressing educational disadvantage. This strategy recognises education as central to breaking cycles of disadvantage, expanding opportunity, and ensuring long-term security. It sets out a more flexible model of support, so that resources are aligned with each school’s level of need as it changes over time.
The strategy also acknowledges that students at risk of educational disadvatage are present in all schools. It therefore focuses on improving outcomes, encouraging innovation, and ensuring schools can access the right supports when needed. latest.question: Deputy Jen Cummins asked the Minister for Education and Youth for an update on the building project for the school (details supplied).
latest.reply:
The major building project for the school referred to by the Deputy is being delivered under the Department's Design and Build Programme which uses a professional external Programme Manager to progress the project through the relevant stages of architectural planning, tender, and construction.
The project will provide a new 1,000 pupil post-primary school, including four classrooms for children with special educational needs, at the permanent school site in Abilene.
The project is currently at Stage 2b, Detailed Design. During this stage, statutory approvals are obtained and the project design is further progressed to reflect any conditions of planning. Planning permission was received from An Bord Pleanála on 25 October 2023. The next stage for this school building project is tender stage.
It is expected that the next tranche of projects to proceed to tender will be published in 2027.
Prioritisation will continue over the coming months to identify this next tranche of projects.
This will be informed by latest available demographic and capacity data, the department’s energy and condition inventory (the validation of which is due to be completed by early 2027), opportunities for phased development to prioritise the most urgent accommodation needs and consultation with school patrons and management bodies.

latest.question: Deputy Roderic O'Gorman asked the Minister for Education and Youth for an update on her Department's plans for the piece of vacant land adjacent to the primary school in the Hollywoodrath estate, Hollystown, Dublin 15; if she can share a potential timeline for the outcome of discussions within her Department in relation to this.
latest.reply:
My department has determined that the Minister-owned site at Hollywoodrath will be the permanent location of Ériu Community College.
The school building on that site is currently occupied by two primary schools while refurbishment works are being carried out on their permanent school buildings. Once these schools return to their refurbished accommodation, the vacated building at the Hollywoodrath site will provide part of the permanent accommodation required for pupils attending Ériu Community College. This is not expected to occur before September 2028.
My department will keep the school authority and patron body informed of progress in relation to this project.
In relation to the balance of the lands at the site and the potential for future school development, my department is aware of planned residential development across North County Dublin. My department will continue to liaise with the local authority and monitor these developments to ensure that school infrastructure planning keeps pace with demographic change.

latest.question: Deputy Charles Ward asked the Minister for Education and Youth whether any new Irish-medium schools are planned for Donegal for the period 2026 to 2031; and her plans to keep up with the demand for Irish-medium schools in Donegal.
latest.reply:
My department establishes new school entities on the basis of identified demographic demand for school places. Demographic requirements in an area determine the need or otherwise for establishing new schools, and the resources available for school infrastructure must be prioritised to meet the needs of areas experiencing significant population growth so as to ensure that every child has access to a school place. Based on current demographic analysis, there are no new school entities currently being established, either Irish-medium or English-medium, in County Donegal. This position is kept under ongoing review by my department.
In planning for school provision, my department divides the country into 314 school planning areas and uses a geographical information system informed by a range of data sources, including Census data, child benefit records, school enrolment trends, residential planning and construction activity, and engagement with local authorities and the construction sector. This enables my department to identify current and future demand for school places and to ensure that school infrastructure planning keeps pace with demographic change.
Where additional capacity is required, this may be provided through the use of existing capacity within schools, the extension of existing schools, or, where warranted by demographic need, the establishment of a new school. In general, my department seeks to meet emerging demand through the expansion of existing schools wherever

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
